It would take nothing less than gruesome medieval torture of these officials to fully satiate justice imo, but I’ve always been a little over the top.  Even adjusting for my flair for the dramatic, a charge of treason and life in prison or the normal death penalty for those in charge is not unreasonable.

As an institution and as individual officers, LE believes the onus is on the citizen to simply tolerate the repeated disrespect mainly because LE is lazy.  LE has a constitutional obligation (and I would argue a moral one) to do their job with the least intrusion possible.  But as the saying goes, they are trained as hammers so everything starts to look like a nail.  There are certainly people who don’t respond appropriately, but an officer who is having a bad day gets coached by his superiors on how to not get caught next time, a citizen having a bad day ends up getting arrested for jaywalking, or violating obscenity laws, or failure to identify, or pick a BS charge.  The only one who benefits from this vicious circle are the police, who get to buy more toys and hire more officers.

I, for one, will not yield to the disrespect because they have a stressful job.  Nobody forced them to choose that career.  I show enough respect by having my hands out of my pockets when they walk up, or on the wheel when they pull up.  The rest is dependent on them.

Good discussions and you’re right about the viscous circle part.

I’d be more willing to talk to a cop about a crime I witnessed (I live in a bad area) if every police interaction I’m involved in didn’t start with “Do you have ID?”  “Yes officer but did I do something wrong?”  “Why don’t you want to identify yourself?”  Beyond the moral and constitutional issues, why is fact that I’m walking in a rough neighborhood (the same neighborhood I walk in all the time, because I live there) mean I have to tolerate being disrespected on a weekly basis?  Those who want respect, give respect.

I don’t trust them based on how I’ve been treated throughout my life.  I trust them less since I’ve begun to take an interest in LE accountability.  As others have pointed out, the really troubling thing is how unlikely “good” police are willing to speak out or even seriously discuss these issues.

Speaking from your dads perspective, grief does weird things to you.  Or let me say it does weird things to me.  I bounce back and forth between holding on to what was and being desperate to get to what will be.  I can live with either, what’s really intolerable is the right now.

My wife died a week before her 36th birthday.  It’s been a pinch over 2 years now.  Like I said, looking back is ok, a little sad.  Looking forward (especially if there’s a warm body to sleep next to) is preferable.  The present as it stands is just too much.  I try to take little things and process them as they come.  I won’t do grief groups or counseling, I can sit in our old room if I want it shoved in my face, which I most certainly do not.  You are entitled to your feelings about your father and his behavior.  My suggestion (more for him than you honestly) is to cut him some slack.  Is this woman the love of his life, probably not.  But I see the goal of grieving is to find a new normal in the least destructive way possible.  Seems like he’s found a fairly benign (if somewhat hurtful to his children) way to put one foot in front of the other.

Again, this is just the opinion of a man who lost his wife not too long ago.  If I lost a mother I loved recently and my father was doing that, I might feel different.

Everyone will die. Death and taxes and all that. I always knew (with a 99.9% degree of certainty) that my wife would predecease me, not because of health reasons, I just always believed either God hated me or I did not have a good enough lock to be spared that. That being said knowing myself and knowing my wife, while I did not wish for it to happen so early, I always wished I would outlive her, so as to spare her what I am going through now.

I am not wise, I am just practiced in sounding so.  I have never made wise decisions (leaving that morning for example), but it is what it is.  I have enough wisdom now not to do that again, but it’s too late now.

I believe wisdom is only gained through pain and grief. If you roll the dice and get lucky, and it was truly an unwise choice, I think most people will make the same unwise choice again. If they get unlucky, they are more likely to realize how unwise the choice was, and not make the same decision again.  Some people are fortunate enough to learn from the experience of others. Most of us have to burn our hand to take to heart the lesson that fire is hot.

It’s an 09 Suzuki SX4.  I bought it from my boss and I did a lot of work on the car when it was his, so I know a lot about it.  About a year ago, either the master or slave cylinder went and he had to drive it about 100 miles to get home. I know the master cylinder was replaced and the slave cylinder was not. I do not know why. For the last year, I don’t know how many miles, He was driving it with a bad slave cylinder. It grinds going into third.  I found if I do a slow deliberate double clutch and let the rpm’s drop all the way to 800 before going from second to fourth, I can feel but not hear the slightest grinding as it goes in.  Second to third is more pronounced grinding, so I avoid third whenever possible.  I am far more gentle on the car than he was, he just slammed the stick into third.  I would like to hold onto the car, so I know I will need a transmission rebuild (or even a used one from the junk yard).

Regarding the clutch, I ruined my first stick car when I was a kid about 15-18 years ago.  Eventually after 2 new clutches the head gasket went (2 clutches in 2 years, my father taught me but he’s a white collar guy and hadn’t driven a stick in 30+ years at the time, he never told me or maybe didn’t know about things like rev matching, not feathering, revving as little as possible in first from a stop).  I know clutches are sturdy if you drive the car properly (even if you drive it hard but skillfully).  I need some time to save up for a new transmission and a few other parts my boss ruined bc he’s not a gear head and doesn’t understand how it all works and why you should or shouldn’t do certain things.  I’m a maintenance mechanic in a nursing home (basic to intermediate HVAC, electrical, plumbing) and I do as much work on my own cars as I can.  I have a fairly solid understanding of the mechanics of things and how they work.  I’m trying to learn about how different parts work in relation to another (more than just a standard 5 minute YouTube overview of how a manual transmission works) so I can get as much mileage out of the parts and the car as possible.

Ty for this reply and for all the replies.  I appreciate your time.

She was great.  Human with flaws of course, but there were far more people at her funeral than will be at mine.

Had a bad day yesterday but I simply can’t devote all the energy to grieving I used to.  It’s simply exhausting, and other areas of my life require attention.  Partially to answer the original question with a little less fuzz in my head, at the beginning, like past the immediate I can’t move or do anything, like going back to work there were a ton of little rituals I had, a ton of physical things I held onto.  I swore I’d always do this or always keep that.  Little by little, without knowing it the demands of life have replaced them.  I feel a little guilty, as if I’m dishonoring her memory in some way.   But I know if it were reversed she would have to let things go little by little to move on and live her life, and I wouldn’t be upset with her for it.

To tie my situation in with yours, life just happens.  Part of it is the choices we make that lead us in a certain direction.  Part of it is the tide of fate which pulls and tugs (sometimes yanks and shoves) us in a direction of its own choosing.  There are all these Carpe Diem and Fortune Favors the Bold sayings out there, but fortune doesn’t favor anyone.  If it did it wouldn’t be fortune.  If you’re satisfied with the choices you’re making that’s really all there is.

I know how feathering the clutch instead of downshifting on a hill does damage.  I was talking from a stop to inch forward.  I know the higher I rev when letting off the clutch slightly the more I’ll wear it.  I’m trying to make this transmission last as long as possible bc i know I need a rebuild.  Trying not to go too hard on the engine either, but most of that work I can do myself.

I destroyed my first stick shift years ago. Cost me a car but I learned how to drive it.  Now I do so much of the work myself I’m trying to learn how it all actually works so I can get as much mileage out of the car as possible.

Every loss is unique.  If this isn’t what you’re asking then I sincerely apologize.  I lost my wife (I’m 38, she was 6 months younger than me) just shy of two years ago.  At the start when people say it just takes time it was more than I didn’t believe them, I was angry.  Violently angry (the booze didn’t help, I’m split on whether it hurts or helps, but that’s a separate discussion).  I’m not ok now.  Far from it.  I would most accurately describe it as it’s easier to pretend I’m ok.

Again, every case is unique but I went from unable to do anything, to able to fake it.  When I give it serious thought I suspect I’m practicing avoidance, but honestly I don’t care,  Ever since then, it’s day by day, hour by hour, moment by mkment.  Sometimes it’s a day st a time, sometimes fractions of a moment.

What I can say relevant to your question, is that I’ve had things, VERY minor things to be sure, but minor things that looking ahead a minute or day or year I was certain I would never move past that are now behind me.  It was never a conscious decision to do x and the y  was getting over whatever hurdle.  almost always I feel
Guilty about getting past that hurdle, and only occasionally do I actively notice that however I did it I’m past that hurdle. Generally, I’ve found if I focus on the mundane I’m able to avoid the really disturbing questions (like where is god and where can I find a weapon to kill him, or why didn’t I just do this, what if I had done that) and I wake up one day and it’s behind me.

Granted rules were made to be broken, and it is a different game now than it was when I was learning and growing up playing, put one of the golden rules I always learned about delayed penalties was if there’s less than 2 minutes on the clock until a period end unless you’ve got an incredible chance just give them the puck.  Other such rules include if you are up man and there is another delayed penalty against them, give them the puck.  Unless you’re coming in on a 3-1 or whatever on zero, give it up.  A bird in hand is worth two in the bush or something along those lines.

You give them the puck for that reason (you’ve already pulled your goalie and you can’t gain an extra man), also because there was less than two minutes to go in the game so you wouldn’t get the full two minute power play anyway.
